content: I want to write a delaborator for a notation. I dont know anything about syntax or parsing, what are some good resources for learning about this? I can provide the notation if that helps.

There's a chapter in the metaprogramming book about delaborators:

https://leanprover-community.github.io/lean4-metaprogramming-book/extra/03_pretty-printing.html
I read through this, but it did not help me much. I am still lost on what syntax is and what this do and let business is.
You can join the weekly #Event announcements > The Meta Café to be less lost :raised_hands:

Perhaps an obvious source, but also maybe overly intimidating to consider at first, is the reference manual chapter on delaborators.

Although hard to read at times, for me it has often cleared up any desired specific details left unsaid in MPIL.

Jeremiah Hockaday said:

I read through this, but it did not help me much. I am still lost on what syntax is and what this do and let business is.

There is no hope to do any meta-programming in Lean if you don’t feel comfortable with do and let. Did you try reading https://leanprover.github.io/functional_programming_in_lean/monads.html?
